habitat: A thornveld bird, usually alone, spending much time in thickets or on the ground under bushes. If disturbed it hops onto a low branch and then into cover.
summary: A common resident. Smaller and less rufous than the other tchagras, more buff-brown. A grey-brown crown and mantle, the crown separated from a whitish eyebrow by a black line, chestnut wings, and pale buff below. The immature is duller. The alarm is a guttural churr. In summer the male flies steeply up and planes down with quivering wings, calling tui-tui-tui-tui-tui in a descending cadence. The Kemp paper name Threestreaked Tchagra and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Black-crowned Tchagra has a black crown. Brown-crowned Tchagra has a grey-brown crown edged by a black line, and it is smaller and more buff-brown.

head.pattern: Grey-brown central crown, separated from a whitish eyebrow by a conspicuous black line. Grey-brown is not a colour token.

upperparts.pattern: Grey-brown mantle. Less rufous and more buff-brown than Black-crowned Tchagra.

wings.pattern: Chestnut wings. The flight pattern is very similar to Black-crowned Tchagra’s, which Newman does not describe further.

Grey-brown and pale buff are described in the pattern. Population figures, the paper name Threestreaked Tchagra and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
